cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: siteId comes from the query string and is used as the Cosmos partition key for the point read, and nothing afterwards compares the permit's tenantId with the caller's tid or checks a site membership, so any authenticated caller who knows a permit id and its site id reads another customer's permit.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: The same item(id, partitionKey).read() shape, but resolveSiteMembership on the caller's own tid gates the read and the document's tenantId is compared with the token's tid afterwards, so the partition key is only used for addressing.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: The status query parameter is concatenated into the Cosmos SQL text as a quoted literal (and sortBy into the ORDER BY clause) while the tenant filter is a bound parameter, so a caller can close the quote and neutralise the c.tenantId predicate in a cross-partition query and read other tenants' permits.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: Same query shape over the same containers, but status is bound as @status, the sort column is looked up in the SORTABLE_COLUMNS allowlist, and the page size is a clamped integer, so no request text reaches the query string.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: runSiteExportNow is registered with authLevel "anonymous" and never validates a token or checks a role, yet it takes tenantId and siteId from the request body and creates an export job (signatures included) whose download path it returns, so any caller who can reach the function app exports any tenant's permit records.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: Also registered authLevel "anonymous", but the handler calls verifyAccessToken and requireRole before writing anything and takes the tenant from the validated token rather than the body, so the missing function key grants nothing.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: The admin decision and the tenant partition key both come from the base64 x-ms-client-principal header, which this app no longer has Easy Auth in front of to inject or strip it, so a caller can present their own principal claiming TenantAdmin in any tenant and rewrite that tenant's site membership roles.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: Decodes the same x-ms-client-principal header, but only to label the audit event; the tenant, the membership check and the role check all come from verifyAccessToken, so the unsigned header decides nothing.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: The client's patch object is spread wholesale over the stored inspection and written back with replace(), so a supervisor can set status to signed_off, forge signedOffBy and signedOffAt, downgrade defectSeverity, or rewrite tenantId - fields the sign-off workflow is supposed to own.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: Same read-merge-replace shape, but the merge iterates the FIELD_PARSERS allowlist instead of the payload keys and rejects anything else with a 400, so status, approvals, tenantId and siteId cannot be reached from the request.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: callbackUrl from the request body becomes the target of a server-side fetch with no scheme, address or host-ownership check, and the response body is echoed back in the 201, so a site admin can make the function app read internal endpoints - the IMDS address, private-endpoint services, the Cosmos account host - and see the answer.

cases.architecture: Azure Functions for Node.js v4 programming model in TypeScript, with Azure Cosmos DB (@azure/cosmos SQL API) as the only data layer, and caller identity taken from a validated Entra ID bearer token, except on the handlers that read the platform-injected x-ms-client-principal header.
cases.why: Fetches a callbackUrl that can also come from the request body, but only after assertDeliverableTarget requires https, rejects address literals and requires the host to sit on a domain the tenant verified by DNS, fetches with redirect "manual", and returns only the status code.
